sources: Israel Central Elections Committee schedule (via Reuters explainer Oct 27, recorded 0800-04) + i24NEWS election-day live blog + ANI (Oct 26 logistics)
fault_line: Security or accountability: does wartime leadership earn another term, or does October 7 demand a change?

sections.what_happened: Polls opened at 07:00 Israel time (09:00 ) for the 120-seat Knesset, the first election since Oct 7 2023 and since Nov 2022; 7,336,553 eligible voters, 12,018 polling stations, ~100,000 election-day workers, NIS 690m budget, free public transport on 660 intercity routes + Israel Railways; IDF detained an Egyptian civilian overnight after he crossed the border fence near Nitzana (i24, single-source, recorded separately as monitor item). No turnout figure, incident or exit poll exists yet at scan time.
sections.what_verified: Reuters (T1) for the 07:00-22:00 Israel schedule; ANI (T1 wire) for the logistics figures; i24NEWS live blog (unregistered, not counted) for voting under way. No result or turnout claim is made.
sections.what_disputed: Final polls disagree: Kan/Channel 12/13 put the opposition at 52-56 vs the Netanyahu bloc at ~50, while Channel 14 gives the Netanyahu bloc 62 (recorded 0600 scan); Palestinian-citizen turnout projected 64-68% (last two polls via Middle East Eye). Polls are not results.
sections.why_matters: 7.3 million Israelis vote on the man who ran the Iran war -- with neither bloc holding 61 seats.
sections.context: Background: POLLS NOW OPEN (09:00 ) -- Israel votes for all 120 Knesset seats; 7,336,553 eligible voters, 12,018 stations; polls 07:00-22:00 Israel time; exit polls after close, final tally Oct 30, official results Nov 4

totw_analysis: Our read: 7.3 million Israelis vote on the man who ran the Iran war -- with neither bloc holding 61 seats. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Security or accountability: does wartime leadership earn another term, or does October 7 demand a change?
